messages.author: a7da442f3527310e
messages.subject: editor support
parts:
For those of us who don't use emacs, I've put together a simple syntax highlighter for .stan files for the Sublime Text 2 editor (github.com/dougalsutherland/sublime-stan; there's a pull request waiting to add this to the package manager thing). These modes are also compatible with Textmate.

There's also a vim mode out there (github.com/mja/vim-stan). It might be handy to put either these files or a pointer to them in the source distribution, along with the emacs StanMode, since, well, they make exactly as much sense to have in there. (My file has an MIT license on it just to have something there, but of course I have no complaints about just dropping it in the repo if it makes sense to include it.)

- Dougal

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] editor support (& contributed licensing issues)
parts:
On 1/15/13 1:07 PM, Dougal Sutherland wrote:
> For those of us who don't use emacs, I've put together a simple syntax highlighter for .stan files for the Sublime Text
> 2 editor (github.com/dougalsutherland/sublime-stan

> <https://github.com/dougalsutherland/sublime-stan/blob/master/Stan.tmLanguage>; there's a pull request
> <https://github.com/wbond/package_control_channel/pull/941> waiting to add this to the package manager thing). These

> modes are also compatible with Textmate.
>
> There's also a vim mode out there (github.com/mja/vim-stan <http://github.com/mja/vim-stan>). It might be handy to put

> either these files or a pointer to them in the source distribution, along with the emacs StanMode, since, well, they
> make exactly as much sense to have in there. (My file has an MIT license on it just to have something there, but of
> course I have no complaints about just dropping it in the repo if it makes sense to include it.)

We've put some thought into licensing issues and
are happy with either of the following two arrangements:

1. You keep the copyright and release it under
an open license (preferably BSD to match Stan,
but other open-source licenses would be OK).

We then redistribute under a contributed directory
that lists the contributors, contributions and licenses.

If there's not too much there, we'd make it part of the
standard source download. Alternatively, we can make separate
downloads for contributed packages.

The only tricky part is accomodating new versions. We can
give people commit priveleges to git or just update with
pull requests.

2. You contribute it to Stan. We license it under BSD
like the rest of Stan and distribute it with Stan.

For this, we do need at least an e-mail from you
explicitly making the contribution and transferring copyright
to the Stan development team.

The Stan copyright is joint among the Stan developers.
We will add developers to the list who make substantial
contributions, but we don't want to be in the situation
where every contributed patch leads to more people on
the developer list (not because we want to hog the credit,
but because we want to keep decision-making easy).

Is one of these two options OK for you to contribute?

Less preferable would be:

3. We just put a note on the web page (and in the doc) directing
people to external tools. I don't like this as much because
it involves maintaining links, which have an annoying tendency
to go stale.

- Bob

messages.author: a7da442f3527310e
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] editor support (& contributed licensing issues)
parts:
I'm happy with either of those options. Since this does need to be maintained in a separate repository in order to support sublime's package manager, though, I think 1 might be a little easier to deal with. The option where this becomes part of Stan proper seems more likely to lead to divergence between the two if future Stan developers tweak the syntax file. Having any development occur elsewhere and the stan or stan-contrib repo occasionally pulling to match the current version seems easier. (Not that I'm anticipating much further development of this, but still.)

Pull requests for updates seem fine, since changes should be infrequent. I just pushed some changes to the readme with installation instructions and relicensing under 3-clause BSD like Stan.

- Dougal
